name: Claude
tagline: Long-context assistant with a developer API built for tool use.
summary: Anthropic's assistant is available as a chat app and as an API. Most Loopwise tutorials use the API because it is easy to script and it handles long documents and structured output well.
goodFor: Summarising and extracting data from long documents
Code review, refactoring and explaining unfamiliar code
Building agents that call your own functions (tool use)
skipIf: You need image generation inside the same product
Your team is locked into another vendor's enterprise contract
pricing: A free plan exists for the chat app. API usage is billed per token, so check the current price list before you budget.

name: ChatGPT
tagline: General-purpose assistant with a large ecosystem around it.
summary: OpenAI's assistant has a wide set of built-in features and the biggest library of third-party integrations. It is a sensible default when you want one tool for many different tasks.
goodFor: Mixed everyday work: writing, analysis, brainstorming
Teams that want the widest choice of integrations
Prototyping with an API that most tutorials already support
skipIf: You want to keep every workflow portable across model providers
You only need one narrow task and a specialist tool does it better
pricing: A free plan exists. Paid plans and API pricing change often, so confirm on the official pricing page.

name: Cursor
tagline: A code editor built around chatting with your codebase.
summary: Cursor is a fork of the VS Code editor with AI features built in: inline edits, codebase-aware chat and multi-file changes. If you already use VS Code, the move is low-friction.
goodFor: Making edits across several files at once
Exploring a codebase you did not write
Developers who already live in VS Code
skipIf: Your company restricts which editors can touch source code
pricing: A free tier exists with limits. Paid plans raise the limits. Check current plans before committing.

name: GitHub Copilot
tagline: Autocomplete and chat that plug into the editor you already use.
summary: Copilot works inside VS Code, JetBrains IDEs and other editors, and integrates with GitHub pull requests. It is the least disruptive way to add AI to an existing team workflow.
goodFor: Teams already on GitHub
Staying in JetBrains or Visual Studio rather than switching editors
Inline completion while you type
skipIf: You want deep, editor-level multi-file refactors as the main feature
Your code can't leave your own infrastructure
pricing: A limited free plan exists and paid individual and business plans add more. Check GitHub's current pricing page.

name: n8n
tagline: Visual workflow automation you can self-host.
summary: n8n connects apps with a node-based editor and lets you drop into code when the visual blocks run out. Because it can be self-hosted, it suits workflows that handle data you don't want to send through a third-party SaaS.
goodFor: Complex branching workflows with custom code steps
Keeping data on your own server
Building AI agents that call several apps
skipIf: You never want to maintain a server and need a fully hands-off tool
Your workflows are three simple steps; a simpler tool is faster to set up
pricing: The self-hosted community edition is free to run on your own server. A paid cloud service is also available.

name: Zapier
tagline: The largest catalogue of app connections, with the lowest setup effort.
summary: Zapier trades flexibility for speed. If an app exists, it probably has a Zapier integration, and a simple automation takes minutes to build.
goodFor: Non-developers who want results in an afternoon
Connecting niche SaaS products
Simple trigger-and-action automations
skipIf: You run high volumes and cost per task matters
You need loops, heavy branching or custom code on every run
pricing: A free plan with limited tasks exists. Paid plans scale with task volume.

name: Make
tagline: Visual automation with more control than Zapier at a lower entry cost.
summary: Make sits between Zapier and n8n: a visual canvas with routers, iterators and data mapping, hosted for you. It rewards people who are willing to learn its data model.
goodFor: Multi-branch scenarios without writing code
Moving structured data between several apps
Budget-conscious automation at moderate volume
skipIf: You want the simplest possible interface
pricing: A free plan exists with monthly operation limits. Paid plans scale with operations.

name: Perplexity
tagline: Answers with sources, built for research rather than conversation.
summary: Perplexity searches the web and returns a cited answer. It is a good first stop for research because you can check every claim against the link beside it.
goodFor: Fast background research with citations
Checking current facts that a plain chat model may not know
Comparing products or reading around a topic
skipIf: You need long-form drafting or code generation as the main task
You can't use a tool that sends queries to a search backend
pricing: A free tier exists and paid plans add more advanced searches. Check the current plans.
